author.heading: About Richard Bach
author.bio: Richard Bach (born 1936) is an American writer whose aviation experiences inform both fiction and nonfiction. Jonathan Livingston Seagull (1970) and Illusions (1977) use flight to explore freedom and perceived limits, blending narrative with philosophical reflection.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: In Illusions, the narrator’s encounter with Donald Shimoda becomes a vehicle for thinking about purpose and possibility. This aphorism treats continued life as an invitation to continue learning and acting. It belongs to Bach’s literary teaching narrative, rather than a documented statement by a historical spiritual teacher.
